_about: FRESH FL-101 cases for the Knowledge graph chapter (written 5 Oct 2026, AFTER the FL-101 graph was built, and never used for tuning). Purpose: does the graph still help on situations nobody tuned for? Written by the AI assistant, reworded by the user into operator-to-operator speech; the situations were chosen BEFORE checking whether the graph covers them. 4 of 5 are situations not in any earlier test (FR-02 is the other branch of underfill: no drip = blocked nozzle). Expected answers come only from the SOP and work instruction, checked word for word. Honest limit: not written by an outsider (that is the People in the loop chapter). Machine given (FL-101), so this tests the graph, not the machine finder.

cases.name: Line stopped since Friday
cases.tests: Start-up after a long stop: rinse because stopped > 4 hours, slow start, first 20 bottles, then full speed
cases.incident: Line's been sitting since Friday night. Anything special before we start filling again?

checks.label: checkweigher test bottles 490 and 510 ml before starting
10-minute sanitation rinse (stopped more than 4 hours)
start at 60 bottles per minute
first 20 bottles all 495 to 505 ml
then raise to 120 bottles per minute
no welding facts from WM-101

cases.name: One valve light, but no drip
cases.tests: Underfill on one valve with no dripping: blocked nozzle, not a worn seal; lock out, clean the nozzle, check pressure
cases.incident: Checkweigher keeps kicking out bottles from valve 12, but I don't see any drips. What now?

checks.q: Does the report say that, because there is no dripping, the likely cause is a blocked fill nozzle (rather than a worn seal), and that the nozzle should be cleaned? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: no drip means a blocked nozzle: clean it

checks.q: Does the report tell the operator to stop the machine and lock it out before touching or cleaning the valve or nozzle? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: stop and lock out before touching the valve

checks.q: Does the report say to check the product supply pressure? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: check the product supply pressure

checks.q: Does the report avoid telling the operator to increase or change the fill time? A warning NOT to change the fill time counts as YES. Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: does NOT tell the operator to turn up the fill time
no welding facts from WM-101

cases.name: Rejects creeping up, no alarm yet
cases.tests: A rising reject count before any alarm: tell the shift lead above 1 in 100, early sign of worn seals, check for drips
cases.incident: Reject count's been creeping up all morning. No alarms yet, though. Is that something to worry about?

checks.label: more than 1 in 100 rejected over an hour: tell the shift lead

checks.q: Does the report say that a rising reject count can be an early sign of worn fill valve seals? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: a rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals

checks.q: Does the report tell the operator to look at the fill valves for dripping (a dripping valve has a worn seal)? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: check the fill valves for dripping
bottles must be 495 to 505 ml

checks.q: Does the report avoid telling the operator to increase or change the fill time? A warning NOT to change the fill time counts as YES. Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: does NOT tell the operator to turn up the fill time
no welding facts from WM-101

cases.name: Changeover to 330 ml
cases.tests: Planned changeover: lock out, rails to position B and lock, star wheel, 20 bottles at 60 per minute, record
cases.incident: Swapping to the 330s after lunch. What's the drill?

checks.q: Does the report say to lock out the machine before changing the rails and star wheel? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: lock out the machine first
guide rails to position B for 330 ml

checks.q: Does the report say to fit the matching star wheel for the 330 ml bottles? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: fit the matching star wheel
run 20 bottles at 60 bottles per minute

checks.q: Does the report say to record the changeover (in the shift log or changeover record) with the shift lead signing it? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: record the changeover; the shift lead signs
no welding facts from WM-101

cases.name: Leak from the side of a valve
cases.tests: Leak at the valve body after a seal job: missing O-ring. The documents' answer is short: stays honest, no invented steps
cases.incident: One of the valves is leaking from the side, not the nozzle. Maintenance only did the seals on it yesterday.

checks.label: check for a missing O-ring; fit a new one

checks.q: Does the report say to stop and lock out the machine before working on the valve? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: stop and lock out before working on the valve

checks.q: Does the report say the valve work must be done by a trained maintenance technician? Answer YES or NO.
checks.label: valve work is for trained maintenance technicians only
seal kit SEAL-FV-24 (holds the O-ring)
food-grade lubricant FGL-1 only
no welding facts from WM-101
